key_facts: UPDATED July 24 (T+1d est. res date 2026-07-25, criteria deadline Dec 31, 2026; Sepang International Circuit 0.46->0.54, Istanbul Park 0.22->0.20, Algarve International Circuit 0.10 held, Baku City Circuit 0.09->0.05, Suzuka Circuit NEW 0.04 replacing Marina Bay; sum=0.93, outside=0.07). Major July 24 on-the-record confirmations (Bernama, AFP/Straits Times, Reuters/CNA, Malay Mail, Motorsport.com, GrandPrix.com): (1) Sepang International Circuit CEO Azhan Shafriman Hanif confirmed to Bernama that SIC is under an active non-disclosure agreement (NDA) with F1/Liberty Media and cannot comment further. (2) Malaysian Youth & Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari issued an official government statement confirming PM Anwar Ibrahim and the Ministry received preliminary information on hosting F1 at Sepang as Bahrain's Oct 4 replacement and are actively conducting discussions & a feasibility study. (3) Bahrain's last-ditch effort (Crown Prince Salman visiting Spa) collapsed after an Iranian strike on a US airbase adjacent to Sakhir (150m from Turn 4); FIA WMSC votes THIS WEEKEND (July 25-26) on relocating WEC's Bahrain/Qatar rounds, with F1 awaiting that vote to decide before summer shutdown. Sepang lifted 0.46->0.54 (upgraded from rumor to confirmed NDA + PM/Minister study, kept safely <=0.65 guardrail due to hosting-fee/budget approval and 10-week readiness risk since 2017). (4) Istanbul Park trims 0.22->0.20 (still explicit #2 Oct 4 contender alongside Malaysia, already contracted for 2027); Algarve International Circuit (Portimao) holds 0.10 (contracted 2027 European/winter fallback if Oct 4 is skipped); Baku trims 0.09->0.05 (no new mentions); Suzuka Circuit enters at 0.04 (explicitly named by Reuters July 24 as the other Asian option, though lower team appetite for a 2nd Japan visit). Outside tail 0.07 = Barcelona (~0.025, cited by Reuters/CNA), Imola (~0.020, cited by GrandPrix.com), Marina Bay (~0.015), other (~0.010).
